content: When rifabutin is coadministered with strong CYP3A4 and CYP2B6 inducers, it increases the metabolism of trazodone, leading to decreased trazodone levels. Exercise caution and monitor the patient closely. Rifabutin reduces the levels or effects of trimethoprim by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Rifabutin increases the metabolism of trimipramine, resulting in decreased levels of the drug. Use caution and monitor the patient. Rifabutin decreases the levels of vilazodone by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Consider increasing the vilazodone dose up to twofold (not exceeding 80 mg/day) if coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inducers for more than 14 days. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of zanubrutinib by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Avoid coadministration of zanubrutinib with moderate CYP3A4 inducers. If unavoidable, increase the zanubrutinib dose to 320 mg orally twice daily. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inducer, resume the previous zanubrutinib dose. Rifabutin reduces the levels or effects of zidovudine by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Apalutamide reduces the levels or effects of rifabutin by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Coadministration of apalutamide, a strong CYP3A4 inducer, with CYP3A4 substrates can result in lower exposure to these medications. Avoid or substitute another drug when possible. Evaluate for loss of therapeutic effect if coadministration is necessary. Adjust the dose according to prescribing information if needed. Rifabutin reduces the levels or effects of apixaban by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. It reduces anticoagulant effects by decreasing systemic exposure to apixaban. Rifabutin reduces the levels or effects of apremilast by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Coadministration with strong CYP inducers significantly decreases systemic exposure to apremilast, potentially resulting in loss of efficacy. Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers can decrease serum concentrations and result in loss of antimalarial efficacy. Reduce the rifabutin dose by up to 75% (e.g., 150 mg every other day or three times per week).
